degree_required.value: Graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody, with at least 90 semester hours of college courses acceptable for credit toward a bachelor's degree
degree_required.quote: has completed at least 90 semester hours of college courses acceptable at the time of completion for credit toward a bachelor's degree at an institution of higher education determined by the department to have acceptable standards; (3) is a graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody

accrediting_body.value: Department-approved podiatry school (may consider Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association)
accrediting_body.quote: In deciding whether to approve or accredit a course of study, training, or education, the department shall consider whether the course is approved or accredited by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education of the American Podiatric Medical Association or its successor organization.

degree_level.quote: is a graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody

school_approval_basis.quote: a podiatry or chiropody school is reputable if: (1) the course of instruction consists of four terms of approximately eight months each, or the substantial equivalent; and (2) the school is approved by the department.

credential_pegged.quote: is a graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody

required.quote: is a graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody; and (4) has successfully completed any other course of training reasonably required by commission rule relating to the safe care and treatment of patients.

experience_source.quote: is a graduate of a reputable school of podiatry or chiropody; and (4) has successfully completed any other course of training reasonably required by commission rule relating to the safe care and treatment of patients.

exams.name: Podiatry License Examination
exams.notes: Written and practical components; must cover anatomy, chemistry, dermatology, diagnosis, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, microbiology, orthopedics, and podiatry as related to ailments of the human foot.
exams.jurisdiction: state (administered or arranged by the department)
exams.quote: each applicant for a license to practice podiatry in this state must pass an examination approved by the department. (b) The department shall recognize, prepare, administer, or arrange for the administration of an examination under this chapter.

interval_years.quote: A license issued under this chapter is valid for one or two years as determined by commission rule.

required.quote: failure to satisfy continuing education requirements

available.quote: On application, the department shall grant a provisional license to practice podiatry to an applicant who: (1) is licensed in good standing as a podiatrist in another state that has licensing requirements that are substantially equivalent to the requirements of this chapter

requirements.value: Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, must have passed a national or other recognized examination, and must be sponsored by a Texas-licensed podiatrist (unless hardship excused). Must also pass Texas examination and verify academic and experience requirements.
requirements.quote: is licensed in good standing as a podiatrist in another state that has licensing requirements that are substantially equivalent to the requirements of this chapter; (2) has passed a national or other examination recognized by the department relating to the practice of podiatry; and (3) is sponsored by a person licensed under this chapter

exists.quote: "Advisory board" means the Podiatric Medical Examiners Advisory Board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Presenting a fraudulently obtained license, certificate, or diploma, or engaging in fraud or deception in passing the examination
disciplinary_grounds.quote: presenting a license, certificate, or diploma that was illegally or fraudulently obtained or engaging in fraud or deception in passing the examination;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being convicted of a drug-related offense under Section 202.606
disciplinary_grounds.quote: being convicted of an offense under Section 202.606;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in habits of intemperance or drug addiction likely to endanger patient health
disciplinary_grounds.quote: engaging in habits of intemperance or drug addiction that in the department's opinion would endanger the health, well-being, or welfare of patients;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in grossly unprofessional or dishonorable conduct likely to deceive or defraud the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: engaging in grossly unprofessional or dishonorable conduct of a character that in the department's opinion is likely to deceive or defraud the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Directly or indirectly violating or attempting to violate this chapter or a rule adopted under it
disciplinary_grounds.quote: directly or indirectly violating or attempting to violate this chapter or a rule adopted under this chapter as a principal, accessory, or accomplice;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using advertising statements tending to mislead or deceive the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: using any advertising statement of a character tending to mislead or deceive the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising professional superiority or the performance of professional services in a superior manner
disciplinary_grounds.quote: advertising professional superiority or the performance of professional service in a superior manner;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Purchasing, selling, bartering, or using a podiatry degree, license, certificate, or diploma
disciplinary_grounds.quote: purchasing, selling, bartering, or using or offering to purchase, sell, barter, or use a podiatry degree, license, certificate, diploma, or a transcript of a license, certificate, or diploma, in or incident to an application for a license to practice podiatry;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Altering with fraudulent intent a podiatry license, certificate, diploma, or transcript
disciplinary_grounds.quote: altering, with fraudulent intent, a podiatry license, certificate, diploma, or a transcript of a podiatry license, certificate, or diploma;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using a podiatry credential that was fraudulently purchased, issued, counterfeited, or materially altered
disciplinary_grounds.quote: using a podiatry license, certificate, or diploma, or a transcript of a podiatry license, certificate, or diploma, that has been fraudulently purchased, issued, counterfeited, or materially altered;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Impersonating or acting as proxy for another person in a podiatry license examination
disciplinary_grounds.quote: impersonating, or acting as proxy for, another person in a podiatry license examination;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Impersonating a license holder or permitting another to use one's license to practice podiatry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: impersonating a license holder, or permitting another person to use the license holder's license to practice podiatry in this state, to treat or offer to treat, by any method, conditions and ailments of human feet;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Employing or associating with a person whose podiatry license has been suspended or who was convicted of unlawful practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: directly or indirectly employing a person whose license to practice podiatry has been suspended or associating in the practice of podiatry with a person whose license to practice podiatry has been suspended or who has been convicted of the unlawful practice of podiatry in this state or elsewhere;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making a material misrepresentation or untrue statement in a license application
disciplinary_grounds.quote: wilfully making in the application for a license to practice podiatry a material misrepresentation or material untrue statement;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being unable to practice podiatry with reasonable skill and safety due to age, illness, substance use, or mental/physical condition
disciplinary_grounds.quote: being unable to practice podiatry with reasonable skill and safety to a patient because of age, illness, drunkenness, or excessive use of drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or other substances or as a result of a mental or physical condition;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to practice podiatry in an acceptable manner consistent with public health and welfare
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failing to practice podiatry in an acceptable manner consistent with public health and welfare;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being disciplined by a professional podiatry association or hospital for unprofessional conduct or professional incompetence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: being removed, suspended, or disciplined in another manner by the podiatrist's peers in a professional podiatry association or society, whether local, regional, state, or national in scope, or being disciplined by a licensed hospital or the medical staff of a hospital

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having repeated or recurring meritorious health care liability claims filed that evidence professional incompetence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: having repeated or recurring meritorious health care liability claims filed against the podiatrist that in the commission's or department's opinion are evidence of professional incompetence likely to injure the public.

definition_quote.value: Podiatry means the treatment of or offer to treat any disease, disorder, physical injury, deformity, or ailment of the human foot by any system or method. The term includes podiatric medicine.
definition_quote.quote: "Podiatry" means the treatment of or offer to treat any disease, disorder, physical injury, deformity, or ailment of the human foot by any system or method.  The term includes podiatric medicine.

methods_authorized.quote: the treatment of or offer to treat any disease, disorder, physical injury, deformity, or ailment of the human foot by any system or method

drug_authority.value: Implicit in podiatric practice; the department provides information on prescribing Schedule II and III controlled substances
drug_authority.quote: prescribing and dispensing pain medications, with particular emphasis on Schedule II and Schedule III controlled substances;

podiatric_assistant_authorized.quote: A podiatrist may delegate to a qualified and properly trained podiatric medical assistant acting under the podiatrist's supervision any podiatric medical act that a reasonable and prudent podiatrist would find within the scope of sound medical judgment to delegate

podiatric_assistant_supervision_level.quote: A podiatrist may delegate to a qualified and properly trained podiatric medical assistant acting under the podiatrist's supervision any podiatric medical act

corrective_footwear_exemption.quote: This chapter does not prohibit the recommendation, advertising, or sale of corrective shoes, arch supports or similar mechanical appliances, or foot remedies by a manufacturer, wholesaler, or retail dealer.
